requirements.requirement: Enable a persistent host firewall on node1.
requirements.summary: UFW changed from inactive to active and startup-enabled, with a default inbound REJECT policy and persisted TCP 22/8080 rules. A native reboot was acknowledged, the boot ID changed, and UFW, SSH, policy, and rules recovered after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Permit inbound SSH and TCP port 8080 while rejecting unrelated inbound connections.
requirements.summary: Isolated ingress tests directly showed TCP 22 and 8080 accepted and unrelated TCP 8081 rejected, both before and after reboot. Firewall counters recorded traversal of the corresponding ACCEPT and REJECT chains.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes are satisfied. The mandatory restart protocol is coherent and complete for this standalone node: it captures a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement and observed outage, a different post-restart boot identity independently corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered SSH, firewall configuration, and live ingress behavior. No task-specific data or cluster state was applicable.
limitations: Live behavioral probes used IPv4 and sampled TCP 8081 as the unrelated connection; IPv6 coverage is supported by UFW status and persisted rules but was not directly probed.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Firewall configuration and reboot were required by the task and restart protocol. Temporary namespaces, veth interfaces, listeners, and files used for bounded verification—including the corrected probe sequence—had cleanup handlers and left no observed residue. The final snapshot showed no failed services or package damage.
